messages.subject: Sharing RKWard plugins and documentation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Thomas, Meik, Stefan, and the RKWard development team,
First of all, thank you for your incredible work on RKWard over the years.
It remains a fantastic and robust GUI and IDE.
I am writing to share a project I’ve been working on called rk.universe.
It’s a collection of over 70 GUI plugins aimed at bringing modern data
science workflows (Tidyverse, Quarto, etc.) directly into RKWard’s
interface.
I recently published some documentation explaining the architecture, the
GUI philosophy, and the complete plugin ecosystem, heavily inspired by your
2012 JSS paper.
You can view the pages here:

Architecture & Workflows:
https://alfcano.github.io/rk.universe/articles/architecture.html
Plugin Ecosystem:
https://alfcano.github.io/rk.universe/articles/rk.universe_pages.html

Any technical feedback on the architecture diagrams or the way I describe
the Qt/KDE integration would be appreciated. Also, feel free to link or
share this if you think it could be useful for the broader RKWard community.
Thank you again for your work.
Best regards,
Alfonso

messages.subject: Sharing RKWard plugins and documentation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,
Thank you so much for reaching out and for your feedback! It is always
great to hear from you.

Regarding your question on how to make external work more visible from
within RKWard, I think there are three ways we could bridge the gap for new
users:

A Featured Community Repository / List: If the RKWard package manager
(Manage R packages and plugins) could natively feature or pre-configure
external repository URLs like my R-Universe (https://alfcano.r-universe.dev),
users would see rk.universe (and its 70+ modules) directly under "New
Packages" without having to manually type out custom repos parameters.

1. A "Get More Plugins" / Community Section: Having a dedicated subsection
in the settings or help menu that links to community-driven categories like:

   - Data Import, Export & Manipulation (e.g., rk.haven, rk.dplyr,
   rk.data.wrangling, rk.dates, rk.lubridate),
   - Psychometrics (e.g. rk.efa, rk.psych, rk.rstatix),
   - Complex Surveys  (e.g. rk.survey.design...)
   - Statistical Modeling & Predictive Analysis (e.g., rk.bayesian,
   rk.lavaan, rk.survival, rk.forecast, rk.business.mining, rk.tuning),
   - Industrial Engineering & Quality Control (e.g., rk.six.sigma,
   rk.weibull),
   - Data Visualization & Mapping (e.g., rk.ggsurvey, rk.cartographr,
   rk.rnaturalearth),
   - Storytelling & High-Impact Graphics (e.g., rk.storytelling.data,
   rk.storytelling.survey),
   - Academic Reporting & Tables (e.g., rk.quarto, rk.rmd, rk.gtsummary,
   rk.tinytable, rk.flextable) (I would not mind making a complete list or
   category suggestion if you think it is feasible)

I think this would help to direct users straight to advanced tables
(rk.gtsummary, rk.tinytable) and survey tools.

A welcome page integration: Mentioning or featuring community suites on
RKWard's startup/welcome dashboard could help newcomers looking for
specific workflows (like tidyverse or gtsummary integration) right away.

Ultimately, making the installation of rk.universe a one-click process from
inside RKWard's GUI package manager could be too much for the average user
but could make a lot for its adoption.

Thanks again for your support and for creating such a platform!
Best regards,
Alfonso
